title: Perplexity Review (2026)
intro: Perplexity is evaluated here as a general-purpose LLM assistant — Perplexity is a cited-search LLM assistant for research, Pro Search, and Deep Research. Free covers basic search with daily Pro/Deep Research caps. Pro is $20/mo or about $17/mo billed annually. Max is $200/mo ($2,000/year) for power-user Labs and Computer credits. Enterprise Pro lists around $40/seat/mo with SSO/admin; Enterprise Max is a higher published seat SKU. Sonar API is a separate usage product. This review uses SoftwareGlimpse’s AI methodology (ease of use, AI job fit, output quality, workflow depth, integrations, governance/privacy, scalability, value, model capability), scoring products inside their job cluster rather than against unrelated peers. It is based on first-party research, not hands-on lab testing.
summary: Choose Perplexity when the LLM job is cited research and Deep Research — not a general Custom GPT workshop.
verdict: Choose Perplexity when the LLM job is cited research and Deep Research — not a general Custom GPT workshop. Compare ChatGPT or Claude for general assistants; Microsoft 365 Copilot for Office-native work. Scores reflect first-party documentation as of 2026-08-18 — not hands-on product testing. Confirm current packaging, usage caps and credit rates on the vendor site before purchase.

criterionAssessments.rationale: Search-first UI is easy for research questions; less of a project/GPT workshop than ChatGPT.
Cited research LLM assistant — a peer inside llm-assistant, not a writing-only or voice tool.
Pro Search and Deep Research with citations are the quality story; not a lab bake-off vs ChatGPT.
Spaces, files, Labs, and Computer (higher tiers) add depth beyond one-shot search.
Slack, API/Sonar, and file Spaces cover research workflows; thinner Office-native depth than Copilot.
Enterprise Pro publishes SSO/admin and no-training claims; consumer tiers are weaker.
Free → Pro → Max → Enterprise ladder exists; Max is expensive for casual teams.
Pro at $20 matches ChatGPT Plus for research-heavy users; Max is a steep step. Affiliate economics excluded.
Model switching on Pro/Max is competitive; capability is research-shaped rather than agent-OS-shaped.

cons: Not the deepest custom-GPT / project OS
limitations: Research/citations are the core — weaker as a general coding or custom-GPT OS
